election._note: The 29 October 2025 election is already in the past at game start (Jan 2026); next scheduled for May 2030 (moved off the usual 4-year mark to avoid clashing with March 2030 municipal elections) — Wikipedia 'Next Dutch general election'

dissolution._note: The cabinet requests a dissolution decree from the King, most often after a coalition partner walks; no codified lockout. Recent practice runs long -- the June 2025 collapse did not reach the polls until 29 October, about four months later, once the Electoral Act's deadlines and the summer recess were accounted for. universiteitleiden.nl, 'Why will elections for Dutch Parliament not be held until November?'.

upper._note: Eerste Kamer, 75 seats, elected by the provincial councils rather than directly. It may only accept or reject a bill in full -- it has no power of amendment and there is no override, so its refusal is final on anything it sees. Grondwet, Arts. 55 and 85; eerstekamer.nl, 'The Senate's role in legislation'.

amendment._note: A revision passes the Tweede Kamer by simple majority in a first reading, then Parliament dissolves for an election, and only the newly elected Tweede Kamer can adopt it, in a second reading, by a 2/3 majority. The intervening dissolution and election are not modelled; the entrenching number, 2/3, is what this rule carries -- already flagged in docs/political-systems.md as not fully modelled. rijksoverheid.nl, 'Herziening van de Grondwet'.
amendment._referendum_note: The Dutch second reading is by a newly elected Tweede Kamer at 2/3; the intervening election is the popular step, and there is no constitutional referendum. rijksoverheid.nl, 'Herziening van de Grondwet'.
amendment._permits_system_change_note: The monarchy is a title in the Grondwet, revisable by the same 2/3 procedure as any other article -- no eternity clause excludes it.

judicial._note: NO judicial review of Acts of Parliament, and the prohibition is EXPRESS rather than doctrinal: Art. 120 of the Grondwet says the constitutionality of Acts of Parliament and treaties shall not be reviewed by the courts. That is a different doctrine from Britain's parliamentary sovereignty and from Switzerland's binding-force clause, and three constitutions reaching one answer by three routes is recorded in docs/judiciary-model.md rather than smoothed over. Grondwet, Art. 120.

formation._note: Formation runs through an informateur and formateur; there is no codified investiture vote. The confidence rule (vertrouwensregel) is constitutional convention, not statute, and a motion carries on a simple majority.

government._pretender_note: Whom data/laws/amendments.json's Restoration Act puts on the throne. Authored per nation because the law is generic and the dynasty is not; a monarchy points this at its own sitting monarch.

fiscal._note: General government, IMF/OECD estimates ~2023-2024, rounded. V1.2a starting policy, derived from France's anchor (see FRA.json): VAT 21% is the Netherlands' own statutory standard rate (Tax Foundation, 'VAT Rates in Europe 2024'). Income and corporate are France's 20/25 scaled by the Netherlands' OECD Revenue Statistics personal/corporate tax-to-GDP share against France's -- the Netherlands leans more on payroll/social contributions than personal income tax and carries a comparatively high corporate-tax base, hence 19/25.8. Spending is France's split scaled by general government expenditure of 44.4% of GDP against France's 57.3% (TheGlobalEconomy.com / OECD Government at a Glance 2025).
